This is a crucial step we need to figure out our standard operating procedure for. We need to follow through with these meetings to get to onboarding. @minhyeong112 I imagine you have the setup to handle these follow ups painlessly?
Historically we only had the actively used `Price: ` labels across other tasks listed. @gentlementlegen we should only populate price labels as needed instead of proactively. 
We've been trying to standardize it across every function and so far this procedure has gotten us through most scenarios. It would have been ideal to break things down into separate tasks with clear deliverables. But I understand this role may be more dynamic than the others. I suppose it would be operationally more efficient to have specialists per function to break down the role further. 
### Conference Standard Operating Procedure
Moving forward I think the following are the productive steps that we may incorporate into the "conference SOP"
- Scout and book relevant meetings via conference app
- Conduct the meetings
- Write and share notes for CRM
- Follow up meeting booked for onboarding.
---
I'm thinking that it would make the most sense to redo and fund this proposal for these steps that provide value to the org. I would consider r&d on process under the umbrella of base pay. In hindsight I would say that the side events planning, although it is a luxury to have, doesn't seem very useful for providing returns on investment when compared to meetings. As such, in the future, perhaps its best that we don't officially do this. 
### Remarks
Perhaps a travel stipend might make sense like with what other larger corporations do. A fixed amount granted for travel purposes. For example $1 per kilometer away from home. 
```
2,091 km
Distance from Seoul to Hong Kong
```
A ~$2000 grant maybe is appropriate to cover the travel costs. Just getting there the `flights + hotel = 1457.97`. However this may not scale well per operator on the team, especially if the team size grows. I suppose it could be for the entire team which would incentivize smaller teams being deployed. 
As for a more extreme example:
```
9,023 km
Distance from Seoul to San Francisco
```
I'm not sure how much the flights were but this trip was incredibly expensive as I recall. I can't find the flights in my credit card statement but looks like I spent $10,089.17 just on my main card in the month of October.

sorry for the delay, no need to take action just yet
pending #165 to smooth out this process 😄

the workflow in this "Business Development" repo is usually like this:
 - someone creates a proposal and adds only a "time" label
 - a manager comes in (aka @0x4007 ) and sets a "priority" label (and maybe adjusts the time label too if he disagrees on the estimate)
 - UbiquityOS comes in a sets the "price" label
 - someone comes in and starts the task (you can write "/start" as a comment to self-assign)
 - that person can write notes, ask questions, collaborate, etc
 - the manager comes back in at the end to mark it "completed" once all questions are answered
This whole workflow is still a work in progress though so it's great to see how it can get smoother! 😄

I've been experimenting extensively on the side to figure this out and I'm almost done
we have the right tools for:
- getting leads
- email
- tg
- linkedin
- x
but none of these integrate well in hubspot.  I'll quickly shift focus to following up with people anyway, and then I'll develop the playbook as quickly as possible
